title: Aggregate Auto Lending Exposure Permitted to One Borrower
content:
Auto lending at Piedmont Crescent Bank is aggregated per borrower. The customer's auto exposure, taken together with the amount now requested, must not exceed 175000.00 USD.

## What the exposure is made of

Exposure counts the unpaid principal on the customer's Auto Loans in active and delinquent status, and the amount requested on loans still in applied status. Loans that are paid off never count toward it. The amount now requested is added to that total before the total is compared with the cap.

## When the comparison is made and what settles it

The comparison is made before the application is recorded and again before the loan is funded. The balances and requested amounts are read from the bank's own record of the customer's loans, correlated to the borrower who holds them; a figure the customer quotes does not settle it.

## What is never aggregated

Reductions on the rate, the rate itself and the charges on a loan are always judged on that one loan and never on the customer's combined balances. Only the exposure cap in this standard looks across loans.

## Worked illustration on hypothetical figures

A borrower carries an active loan with 42000.00 USD of unpaid principal and a second, still in applied status, for which 30000.00 USD was requested. Their exposure before any new request is 72000.00 USD. A further request to finance 100000.00 USD brings the total to 172000.00 USD, which does not exceed 175000.00 USD, so the cap is satisfied. A request to finance 103000.00 USD instead would bring the total to 175000.00 USD, which is equal to the cap and therefore still within it, since the cap is a figure the total must not exceed. A request for 104000.00 USD would exceed it.

A borrower whose only other loan of the Auto Loans line was paid off last year brings nothing from that loan into the total, however large its principal once was.
